organism_context: Azoarcus evansii and other bacteria using the aerobic CoA-dependent 'box' benzoate pathway (~4-5% of sequenced bacteria)
rationale: BoxC is a homodimeric crotonase (enoyl-CoA hydratase/isomerase) superfamily protein that performs one overall ring-cleavage: it uses two waters to open the 2,3-epoxide/oxepin ring and then hydrolyse ring C2 off as formate, all in one active site, so this is a single catalytic activity (the term 'dihydrolase' refers to the two waters, not to two enzymes' worth of activity).
direction_note: The published stoichiometry (dihydrodiol/epoxide + 2 H2O -> 3,4-dehydroadipyl-CoA semialdehyde + formate) matches the equation read left-to-right; recondensing formate onto the semialdehyde to rebuild the ring is not an activity BoxC has.

organism_context: Streptomyces spp.; an isochorismatase-like hydrolase (ILH) superfamily resistance/self-protection enzyme
rationale: SttH is a single-activity ILH-superfamily hydrolase that opens the streptolidine lactam ring of streptothricin antibiotics, inactivating them; no second catalytic activity is reported for it.
direction_note: Lactam hydrolysis to the ring-opened acid is the antibiotic-inactivating step and runs one way; no lactam-forming (ring-closing) activity is known for SttH.

organism_context: Bradyrhizobium sp. strain JS329 (5-nitroanthranilic acid degradation); a metalloprotease-family (amidohydrolase-like) protein repurposed for aromatic deamination
rationale: 5NAA-A catalyses the single hydrolytic deamination of 5-nitroanthranilate to 5-nitrosalicylate by transition-metal-dependent nucleophilic aromatic substitution; the structural/mechanistic work describes one active site and one activity.
direction_note: Hydrolytic release of ammonia from the ring is irreversible; re-amination of 5-nitrosalicylate is not an enzymatic reaction.

organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus (staphyloxanthin pathway) and other C30-carotenogenic Firmicutes/Lactobacillaceae
rationale: A single CrtN polypeptide, an FAD-dependent amine-oxidase-fold desaturase, introduces the successive double bonds; iterative use of one active site on a series of substrates is not a second catalytic activity. This entry is the summed four-desaturation (dehydrosqualene -> 4,4'-diapolycopene) that IUBMB assigns to the one EC 1.3.8.2.
direction_note: The flavin is CrtN's prosthetic group, not a free cosubstrate; writing four free FAD/FADH2 and omitting the terminal oxidant makes the desaturation look uphill, whereas in vivo reoxidation of the bound flavin pulls the reaction one way into carotenoid biosynthesis.

organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus and other C30-carotenogenic Firmicutes; first of the three/four successive desaturations
rationale: Raisig and Sandmann showed the three double bonds of the S. aureus C30 pathway are introduced by a single purified enzyme; CrtN is a one-activity flavoprotein desaturase and remains the sole target of the naftifine/benzofuran CrtN inhibitor series.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for CrtN's bound flavin plus its (omitted) terminal oxidant, which is what actually makes each desaturation one-way in vivo.

organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus and other C30-carotenogenic Firmicutes; second of the successive desaturations
rationale: Same single CrtN polypeptide acting iteratively; one catalytic activity, confirmed by purification of the enzyme catalysing all three desaturations.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for CrtN's bound flavin plus its (omitted) terminal oxidant, which is what actually makes each desaturation one-way in vivo.

organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus and other C30-carotenogenic Firmicutes; third of the successive desaturations (to 4,4'-diaponeurosporene)
rationale: Same single CrtN polypeptide acting iteratively; one catalytic activity.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for CrtN's bound flavin plus its (omitted) terminal oxidant, which is what actually makes each desaturation one-way in vivo.

enzyme_name: 4,4'-Diapophytoene (dehydrosqualene) desaturase CrtN (CrtN/CrtNb for the fourth desaturation)
organism_context: Staphylococcus aureus and relatives; the fourth desaturation (diaponeurosporene -> diapolycopene), run by CrtN itself or a CrtN paralogue depending on strain
rationale: Whichever paralogue performs this step, it is a one-activity FAD-dependent desaturase of the same family; no second catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: Free FAD/FADH2 stands in for the bound flavin plus the omitted terminal oxidant; carotenoid desaturation does not run backwards in vivo.

distinct_activities: oxepin-CoA hydrolase, C-terminal (R)-specific enoyl-CoA hydratase/MaoC-like ring-cleaving domain (EC 3.3.2.12)
NADP+-dependent 3-oxo-5,6-didehydrosuberyl-CoA semialdehyde dehydrogenase, N-terminal ALDH domain (EC 1.2.1.91)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other aerobic phenylacetate degraders; a natural ALDH+MaoC gene fusion. In bacteria lacking the fusion the two activities are encoded by separate genes (an NAD+-ALDH in the paa cluster plus a hydratase outside it).
rationale: Teufel et al. characterised PaaZ explicitly as a bifunctional fusion protein: the C-terminal hydratase domain cleaves the oxepin ring to a highly reactive aldehyde and the N-terminal NADP+-ALDH domain oxidises that aldehyde to 3-oxo-5,6-dehydrosuberyl-CoA.
direction_note: This ModelSEED entry covers only the hydrolase half of the bifunctional enzyme; the reactive semialdehyde it produces is immediately consumed by PaaZ's own ALDH domain (otherwise it cyclises to a dead-end tropone precursor), so the ring-opening is pulled forward in vivo and never runs backwards.

organism_context: Characterised as NADP+-farnesol dehydrogenase in Helicoverpa armigera (juvenile-hormone pathway) and NAD(P)+-farnesol dehydrogenase in Polygonum minus; the reductase running the opposite direction is a separate SDR
rationale: The ModelSEED entry carries no EC and no cofactor, so the catalyst is inferred from the chemistry; the characterised farnesol/farnesal oxidoreductases are single-activity short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase enzymes.
direction_note: The equation drops NAD(P)+/NAD(P)H entirely (ModelSEED flags charge imbalance -2, i.e. the missing hydride), so the direction here is set by the pyridine-nucleotide pool and by which of the two distinct enzymes (dehydrogenase vs reductase) is present, not by any one protein.

organism_context: Actinosynnema pretiosum (ansamitocin/ansamitocinoside post-PKS tailoring)
rationale: Asm21 carbamoylates two different hydroxyls (C-7 of the polyketide core and the 4''-OH of the glucosyl moiety), but that is one carbamoyl-transfer activity used iteratively on two acceptors, which is promiscuity/iteration rather than a second catalytic activity (compare the homodimeric iterative CTase GdmN).
direction_note: Carbamoyl transfer from carbamoyl phosphate releases inorganic phosphate from a high-energy mixed anhydride, so the biosynthetic (carbamoylating) direction is effectively irreversible.

organism_context: Bacteria (GlgA) and eukaryotes (GYS). Note the ModelSEED entry lumps four ECs - 2.4.1.11 glycogen synthase, 2.4.1.12 cellulose synthase, 2.4.1.34 1,3-beta-glucan synthase, 2.4.1.168 xyloglucan glucosyltransferase - each of which is itself a separate single-activity glucosyltransferase.
rationale: Glycogen synthase is a single-activity retaining glycosyltransferase; chain branching is done by a different protein (GlgB/GBE) and glycogenin's self-glucosylation is a different gene product, so neither makes GlgA/GYS bifunctional. Called from established biochemistry rather than a dedicated literature search.
direction_note: ModelSEED reduced the reaction to 'UDP-glucose -> UDP' and lost the glucan acceptor (status MI:C:-6/H:-10/O:-5), so the stored dG is for a half-reaction; glucosyl transfer from UDP-glucose onto the growing glucan is strongly exergonic and one-way (glycogen breakdown goes via phosphorylase, not by reversal).

organism_context: Coptis japonica, Papaver somniferum and other benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid-producing plants
rationale: CNMT is a single-activity SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase; cloning/purification and the crystal structure describe one catalytic site and one (broad-substrate) methyl-transfer activity, with no demethylase or other second activity.
direction_note: SAM-dependent N-methylation with release of S-adenosylhomocysteine is essentially irreversible; the reverse (SAH + N-methylcoclaurine -> SAM + coclaurine) is not an activity of this enzyme.

distinct_activities: gamma-glutamylcysteine transpeptidation onto glutathione/phytochelatin acceptors (phytochelatin synthesis, EC 2.3.2.15)
papain-like cysteine-peptidase processing (deglycination) of glutathione S-conjugates
organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis PCS1/CAD1), algae, some invertebrates and Schistosoma mansoni; the cyanobacterial homologue NsPCS (Nostoc) retains only the peptidase activity and cannot make phytochelatins
rationale: One papain-like catalytic-Cys domain carries both the gamma-Glu-Cys transpeptidation that builds phytochelatins and a distinct hydrolytic processing of glutathione S-conjugates in xenobiotic metabolism; both are genuine catalysis (not moonlighting), though they share the same nucleophile, which is why I call this medium rather than high.
direction_note: ModelSEED collapsed the reaction to 'GSH -> glycine' and dropped the gamma-Glu-Cys acceptor (status MI:C:-8/H:-10/N:-2/O:-4/S:-1), so no direction can be read from the stored thermodynamics; the enzyme runs in the glycine-releasing, phytochelatin-forming direction.

enzyme_name: Peptidoglycan glycosyltransferase of a class A penicillin-binding protein (PBP1a/PBP1b)
organism_context: Class A PBPs of E. coli, S. aureus, enterococci etc. carry both activities on one chain. The same EC 2.4.1.129 step is also catalysed by genuinely monofunctional GT51 glycosyltransferases (MtgA/MGT) and by the unrelated SEDS polymerases RodA/FtsW, so the reaction is not intrinsically bifunctional.
rationale: The dominant catalysts of lipid II polymerisation in most bacteria are class A PBPs, single polypeptides with an N-terminal GT51 glycosyltransferase domain and a C-terminal transpeptidase domain - two distinct catalytic activities, not a multi-subunit complex.
direction_note: The growing glycan acceptor is missing from the equation (status MI:C:-39/H:-63/N:-8/O:-19), leaving only 'lipid II -> undecaprenyl-PP'; polymerisation with release of undecaprenyl-pyrophosphate is irreversible, and depolymerisation is done by unrelated lytic transglycosylases.

enzyme_name: Dolichyl-diphosphate:polyphosphate phosphotransferase (EC 2.7.4.20) - catalysing protein not identified
rationale: I could find no literature identifying a protein for EC 2.7.4.20 in PubMed or Europe PMC; the well-characterised activity that converts Dol-PP to Dol-P is a dolichyl-pyrophosphate phosphatase (DOLPP1/CWH8-type) that releases free Pi rather than transferring it onto polyphosphate, so the enzyme behind this specific entry is genuinely unknown and I am not defaulting it to monofunctional.
direction_note: The polyphosphate phosphate acceptor is absent (status MI:H:-1/O:-3/P:-1), which is why both estimators return a ~208 kJ/mol dG; whatever runs it, dolichyl-PP is dephosphorylated to dolichyl-P to recycle the glycan carrier, never the reverse.

organism_context: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 and other cyanobacteria (intracellular CphB); Pseudomonas alcaligenes DIP1 (extracellular CphEal)
rationale: Cyanophycinase is a single-activity serine-type exopeptidase that hydrolyses cyanophycin to beta-Asp-Arg dipeptides; polymer synthesis is a separate ATP-dependent enzyme (cyanophycin synthetase CphA), so the two activities are on different proteins.
direction_note: The cyanophycin polymer substrate is missing - the equation is literally 'H2O <-> beta-Asp-Arg' (status MI:C:10/H:17/N:5/O:4) - so the stored dG is meaningless; hydrolysis is the only direction cyanophycinase runs.

enzyme_name: Aurone-synthase-type polyphenol oxidase (presumed); this entry is a radical intermediate step inside the catalytic cycle, not a standalone enzyme reaction
organism_context: MetaCyc PWY-6401 (hispidol biosynthesis); the characterised relative is snapdragon aureusidin synthase AmAS1, a chalcone-specific polyphenol oxidase homolog
rationale: 'phenoxy radical VII' and 'QVE' are two same-formula (C15H10O5) enzyme-bound mechanism intermediates rather than free metabolites, and I could not confirm which protein is credited with this individual step; for the record, the characterised aureusidin synthase does carry two chemically distinct activities (B-ring 3-hydroxylation followed by oxidative cyclisation) at one binuclear copper centre, but I will not stamp that onto this unidentified sub-step.
direction_note: A single radical rearrangement lifted out of a polyphenol-oxidase catalytic cycle has no standalone in vivo direction; MetaCyc gives it no EC and placeholder compound names, and ModelSEED flags it charge-imbalanced (CI:1).

enzyme_name: PLP-dependent gamma-family cystathionine lyase/synthase running gamma-replacement with water (cystathionine gamma-lyase CTH/CGL, or cystathionine gamma-synthase MetB)
rationale: The stoichiometry here (cystathionine + H2O -> cysteine + homoserine) is a gamma-replacement by water, not the canonical gamma-lyase reaction (which gives 2-oxobutanoate + ammonia), so the catalyst is inferred from chemistry rather than confirmed; every gamma-family PLP enzyme that could run it (CGL, CGS, CBL) is a single-activity homotetramer with one PLP site per subunit.
direction_note: Cystathionine is built in vivo from an O-activated homoserine (O-succinyl- or O-acetyl-homoserine), never from free homoserine, so ModelSEED's direction (homoserine + cysteine -> cystathionine + H2O) is a reaction no enzyme runs; the cleavage direction is the real one.

organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain B13 and other chloroaromatic degraders using the modified ortho-cleavage pathway
rationale: Dienelactone hydrolase is the textbook single-domain alpha/beta-hydrolase with one Cys-His-Asp catalytic triad and one activity (lactone hydrolysis to maleylacetate); no second catalytic function is reported.
direction_note: Lactone ring hydrolysis is one-way for this enzyme (it has no lactonising activity), and the product is pulled off by maleylacetate reductase downstream.

enzyme_name: FeMo-cofactor maturation machinery (NifB, NifEN, NifH, NifQ, NifU, NifV) - no single enzyme catalyses this entry
organism_context: Azotobacter vinelandii and other diazotrophs
rationale: FeMo-co assembly is a multi-step, multi-protein maturation pathway - radical-SAM NifB makes the NifB-co/L-cluster, the NifEN scaffold inserts Mo and homocitrate with NifH, NifQ/NifU supply Mo and Fe-S - so there is no one polypeptide whose functionality can be classified; the honest answer is a pathway, not an enzyme.
direction_note: Cofactor assembly runs one way (precursors -> FeMo-co), but the entry also mis-states the chemistry by consuming N2 and emitting NH3 (that belongs to nitrogenase catalysis, not cofactor assembly) and is mass/charge imbalanced, so no direction call from this equation is physically meaningful.

organism_context: Plants (Arabidopsis APR1-3) and green algae; the plant enzyme carries an N-terminal reductase domain plus a C-terminal glutaredoxin-like domain
rationale: Suter et al. showed the 'APS sulfotransferase' that yields S-sulfoglutathione and APS reductase are the same protein; the C-terminal glutaredoxin-like domain is an internal GSH-dependent electron-transfer module serving that one reductase activity rather than a second substrate-level catalysis, so I call it monofunctional rather than bifunctional.
direction_note: APS is a high-energy phosphosulfate mixed anhydride, so transfer of its sulfo group to glutathione with release of AMP is irreversible; in vivo the same enzyme goes further and releases free sulfite plus GSSG, draining it still harder forward.

organism_context: Pseudomonas putida TW3 (4-nitrobenzoate degradation via 4-hydroxylaminobenzoate)
rationale: PnbB is the single-activity lyase of the pnb operon that converts 4-hydroxylaminobenzoate to protocatechuate with release of ammonia; the upstream nitroreductase (PnbA) and downstream ring-cleavage enzymes are separate gene products.
direction_note: The Bamberger-type rearrangement/hydrolysis of the hydroxylamino intermediate is irreversible; nothing aminates protocatechuate back to 4-hydroxylaminobenzoate.

enzyme_name: Not identified (nominally a triazine amidohydrolase of the Atz/Trz amidohydrolase superfamily)
organism_context: Atrazine catabolism (Pseudomonas sp. ADP AtzA/AtzB/AtzC and relatives)
rationale: The two triazines in this entry carry different N-alkyl substituents - deisopropylhydroxyatrazine is C5H9N5O (N-ethyl) and N-isopropylammelide is C6H10N4O2 (N-isopropyl) - so no single hydrolytic step interconverts them, and I could find no enzyme credited with this transformation; calling any functionality here would be fabrication.
direction_note: The substrate/product pair is mismatched (ethylamino- vs isopropylamino-triazine) and patched up with CO2/NH3, with ModelSEED flagging charge imbalance -6, so neither direction describes a real enzymatic step.

enzyme_name: Unassigned reductive dechlorination step (MetaCyc PWY-5370, carbon tetrachloride degradation I); comparable chemistry is done by corrinoid cofactors and by organohalide-respiring reductive dehalogenases (RdhA)
organism_context: Carbon tetrachloride / chloromethane degradation; anaerobic Dehalobacter enrichments biodegrade chloroform and dichloromethane, but no protein is assigned to this specific CH2Cl2 -> CH3Cl step in the pathway this entry comes from
rationale: Sequential reductive dechlorination of chloromethanes in this pathway is frequently corrinoid/thiol-mediated and partly abiotic, and I could not identify a specific protein for this step, so the catalyst - and hence its functionality - is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: The two-electron donor is missing (ModelSEED flags charge imbalance -2); whatever supplies the electrons, reductive dechlorination only ever runs toward the less-chlorinated product, so chloromethane + Cl- -> dichloromethane is not a reaction.
